newsitem.title: USA: St. Paul says "comfortable" with Nuveen.
newsitem.headline: St. Paul says "comfortable" with Nuveen.

text.p: St. Paul Cos Inc said it was "very comfortable with our relationship" with John Nuveen Co, the investment banking and mutual fund company.

St. Paul, the property liability insurer that owns about 77 percent of outstanding Nuveen common shares, declined to comment on a report it may sell its controlling stake. "We don't comment on rumors that arise in the marketplace," a spokesperson said.
A Nuveen spokesman said there were no talks ongoing to sell or merge the company, and no desire by Nuveen to have such talks.

St. Paul owns 100 percent of Class B common stock, or about 25 million shares, according to a Nuveen spokesman. Another 7.5 million Class A common are also outstanding, the spokesman said, but St. Paul does not own those shares.
Last week Nuveen said it was buying back back about 3.5 million of the Class A and Class B shares in the open market and in private transactions.
